\begin{abstract}
Idle agent sessions hold key-value (KV) cache memory on the GPU.
We cut the p95 time to first token (TTFT) to 0.66 of a recency baseline.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:intro}
An idle session keeps its key-value (KV) cache on the GPU.
The time to first token (TTFT) grows when that cache is gone.
Kwon et~al.~\cite{vllm} page the cache, and SGLang~\cite{sglang} adds a disk tier.
Each GPU holds 80\,GB, a block holds 16~MB and a restore takes 3\,ms.
Runs 1--4 use the same node and the 1990s design is not in scope.
We pick recency rather than size for the first tier.
The gap is statistically significant (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, $p < 0.01$).
The engine's queue is short, and ``Ask the Tool, Don't Guess'' is a paper title.
Math is skipped: $a - b$ and $x --- y$ are fine.
Figure~\ref{fig:trace} shows the trace and Table~\ref{tab:pools} lists the pools.
Section~\ref{sec:intro} and~\ref{sec:part} use \cref{tab:pools} as well.
Latency is in milliseconds (ms) throughout.
